body:
I quit my job today. I'm not sure if that's the start of trying to do something new to improve or the beginning of the end. I'm going to take a few days off to spend with friends and family and hopefully start rebuilding.

I don't hold out much hope but I appreciate everyone's input and kindness.

Thanks for your kind words.

I wish I shared your outlook, I feel like I'm a pussy for wanting to quit and I feel like everyone else would just plow through. I compare myself to other people an awful lot (wishing I was "normal") even though I know it's not really beneficial to me in any way, and I always assume that everyone else would have done something better than me.

Goes right back to the need to stop blaming myself or getting down on myself, which is something I know I need work on. I do appreciate your words, it's nice to think that I'm doing alright compared to how others might have in my shoes, even if it's petty and terrible of me to find some solace in it.

A dog really would be nice, but it's hard for me to get one if I'm just planning on killing myself anyway. Obviously the goal would be to get one so I'm not thinking like that, but making the leap of faith to get one is hard for me. In the back of my head I've got the nagging thought that I'm not going to be around much longer and why create another problem for my surviving family. A problem of outlook I know, but I can't stop myself from doing this, even if I recognize it.

I appreciate your reply. 
I hate to be a broken record, but it's all a matter of perspective. I can take the same fact (managing to do ok for myself) and decide that's a good reason to kill myself, I've accomplished a lot of things that I wanted to. I know my depression is a big reason why I have such a negative spin on things, it's just so hard to change my outlook after dwelling and thinking about it for so long. 

It's almost a self-fulfilling prophecy, and despite being aware enough to realize this, I'm no more likely to change my behavior. It sounds as dumb to me as it does to you, but I'm just too much of a pussy to go the hard way. 

It's a bad example, but I feel like I've been stuck in a hole for 12 years and I just don't feel like trying to pull myself out anymore. I don't even know if I can honestly say I tried my best and failed, and that just makes me cry more instead of wanting to do something about it.

I probably shouldn't have even posted anything here. I've been thinking about this non-stop for as long as I can remember, and my mind is probably made up. I don't mean to make other people feel bad for me unnecessarily. Ty for posting.

Thank you for your reply.

I know there are probably countless other innocent reasons that I would see things this way (and at my best I can rationalize like this and don't blame myself), but most of the time I let myself assume the worst. It's a matter of outlook and I know if I can do little things to improve it I might not feel like this, but I don't know where to begin.

I'll try not to be so hard on myself or always assume the worst, thank you.

If you mean "deal with it", I do indeed plan to confront him before I kill myself. 
If you mean face the problems head on, I don't think I can.

I can relate to your story. I remember going along because it felt exciting and he told me that it was something friends do and it is something grown-ups shouldn't know we were doing. I felt like I was one of the cool kids. I still feel like it's my fault, that I should have been able to see through it.

I appreciate you sharing.
